title: Where Claude Code MCP servers are configured and how their tools are named
what: MCP servers come from four places: project `.mcp.json`; `~/.claude.json` top-level `mcpServers` (user scope); `~/.claude.json` `projects["C:/path/with/forward/slashes"].mcpServers` (local scope); and plugins enabled in `enabledPlugins` (`~/.claude/settings.json` plus the project's `.claude/settings*.json`), whose installPath is in `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` and whose servers are in `.mcp.json` (with or without the `mcpServers` wrapper) or in `plugin.json`.
why: The tool names go into subagent allowlists, so they must match exactly what Claude Code generates.
learned: Plugin server tools are named `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>`, as seen in real transcripts (`mcp__plugin_monet_monet__`). Servers injected by the desktop app (claude-in-chrome, Claude_Browser, computer-use, ccd_*) appear in no config file, so the user must add them by name. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR moves both `.claude.json` and the settings.
author: reactive-end
